When the rains failed in a particular village, a group of people left to seek other opportunities. Many of them ended up in the United States, with the result that a subsequent migrant from the same village would have connections in the US who were securely employed and able to help him or her find a job. He expected to see more migrants, more employed migrants, and better-paid migrants. This is exactly what the data showed. Network connections matter.

❌ ① firmly(단단히): securely의 유의어
❌ ② steadily(꾸준히): securely의 유의어
✅ ③ precariously(불안정하게): securely의 반의어로 가장 적절
❌ ④ solidly(견고하게): securely의 유의어
det.tip: securely(안정적으로) ↔ precariously(불안정하게)

questions.passage:
(A) The scientist studied the properties of <u>matter</u> in the physics laboratory. Every object around us is made up of tiny particles of physical <u>matter</u>.

(B) Having friends abroad truly helps new migrants. As Kaivan Munshi showed, network connections <u>matter</u> more than people realize.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)의 밑줄 친 matter의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A)의 matter는 명사로 '물질(physical matter)', (B)의 matter는 동사로 '중요하다(be important)'.
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 물질 — (B) 중요하다: (A)는 physical matter(물질), (B)는 network connections matter(중요하다)
❌ ② (A) 중요하다 — (B) 물질: 의미가 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ (B)가 '문제'가 아니라 '중요하다'
❌ ④ (A)가 '중요하다'가 아니라 '물질'
det.tip: matter: 명사 '물질/문제', 동사 '중요하다'. 품사로 의미 구분

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a long period of dry weather when there is not enough rain"

det.korean: drought = 가뭄 (비가 충분히 내리지 않는 긴 건조한 기간)
det.analysis:
❌ ① migrant(이주자): 사람이지 날씨 현상이 아님
❌ ② village(마을): 장소이지 날씨가 아님
❌ ③ weather(날씨): 일반적 개념으로 정의에 부합하지 않음
✅ ④ drought(가뭄): 비가 부족한 긴 건조 기간이라는 정의에 정확히 부합
det.tip: drought = 가뭄

questions.passage: He __________ (expect) to see more migrants, more employed migrants, and better-paid migrants. This is exactly what the data showed. Network connections matter.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

expect → ____

det.korean: 그는 더 많은 이주자, 더 많은 고용된 이주자, 그리고 더 높은 임금을 받는 이주자를 보게 될 것으로 '예상했다'.
det.analysis: 주어 He + 과거시제 문맥(compared, had had 등 앞에서 과거 사용) → 동사 expect를 과거형 expected로 변환. He expected to see... 가 문맥상 자연스러움.
det.tip: expect(예상하다)의 과거형은 expected. 과거시제 문맥에서 동사 변환 필수

questions.passage: Many of them ended up in the United States, with the result that a subsequent migrant from the same village would have connections in the US who were securely __________ (employ) and able to help him or her find a job.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

employ → ____

det.korean: 동일한 마을에서 뒤이어 이주하는 사람은 미국에 안정적으로 '고용된' 인맥을 갖게 되었다.
det.analysis: 관계대명사 who + be동사(were) 뒤에서 수동 분사가 필요. 주어(connections)가 '고용되는' 대상이므로 과거분사 employed(수동)로 변환. who were securely employed = 안정적으로 고용된.
det.tip: be + p.p. = 수동태. 사람이 회사에 '고용되는' 것이므로 employed(과거분사) 필수

questions.passage: Professor Kaivan Munshi observed that, regardless of the opportunities in the United States, __________ such as heavy rain pushed people out of Mexico. When the rains failed in a particular village, a group of people left to seek other opportunities. Many of them ended up in the United States, with the result that a subsequent migrant from the same village would have connections in the US who were securely employed and able to help him or her find a job. Kaivan predicted that if one compared two villages in Mexico with the same weather in a given year, but one of them had had a drought in previous years while the other had not, it would be easier for a resident of the village with drought to find a job than for the resident of the village without a drought. He expected to see more migrants, more employed migrants, and better-paid migrants. This is exactly what the data showed. Network connections matter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 자연재해(natural disasters). 미국 내 기회와 상관없이 폭우와 같은 '자연재해'가 사람들을 멕시코에서 떠나게 했다는 문장의 주어.
det.analysis:
✅ ① natural disasters(자연재해): 'such as heavy rain'이라는 예시가 뒤따르므로 '자연재해'가 정확히 부합 (natural disasters such as heavy rain)
❌ ② other opportunities(다른 기회): 뒷 문장에서 사람들이 '찾아 떠난 것'이지 사람들을 떠밀어낸 원인이 아님
❌ ③ heavy rain(폭우): heavy rain은 뒤따라 나오는 '예시'이므로 빈칸에 들어갈 상위 개념이 필요
❌ ④ previous years(이전 몇 년): 글 후반 Kaivan의 비교 문맥에 쓰이는 표현으로 도입부와 불일치
det.tip: natural disasters such as heavy rain = 폭우와 같은 자연재해 (상위 개념 + 예시)

questions.passage: Professor Kaivan Munshi observed that, regardless of the opportunities in the United States, natural disasters such as heavy rain pushed people out of Mexico. When the rains failed in a particular village, a group of people left to seek other opportunities. Many of them ended up in the United States, with the result that a subsequent migrant from the same village would have connections in the US who were securely employed and able to help him or her find a job. Kaivan predicted that if one compared two villages in Mexico with the same weather in a given year, but one of them had had a drought in previous years while the other had not, it would be easier for a resident of the village with drought to find a job than for the resident of the village without a drought. He expected to see more migrants, more employed migrants, and better-paid migrants. This is exactly what the data showed. __________ matter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 관계망 연결(Network connections). 글 전체의 결론: 미국 내 이미 고용된 이주자 인맥이 후속 이주자의 취업을 돕는다는 논지.
det.analysis:
❌ ① subsequent migrant(뒤이은 이주자): 이주자 자신이 아니라 이주자를 돕는 주체가 빈칸 주어
❌ ② employed migrants(고용된 이주자): Kaivan이 예상한 '결과' 항목이지 글 전체의 결론 주어가 아님
❌ ③ better-paid migrants(더 높은 임금의 이주자): Kaivan의 예상 결과 항목이지 결론 주어가 아님
✅ ④ Network connections(관계망 연결): 글의 마지막 문장 'Network connections matter.'가 전체 결론
det.tip: Network connections matter = 관계망 연결이 중요하다 (글의 주제문)
